titles: RRSP for the Self-Employed in Canada: What $5,000 Really Saves
Self-Employed? Your RRSP Saves Less Than You Think
yt.description:
Self-employed in Canada and thinking about an RRSP? Here's what a $5,000 contribution really does to the tax bill.

Example (2026, Manitoba, single, $60K net self-employment income, enough RRSP room): taxable income drops by $5,000. Federal tax −$700, Manitoba tax −$637.50. The bill goes from about $16,106 to $14,768: about $1,338 saved, roughly 27¢ per dollar. Not 36¢, because self-employed CPP is based on business income and doesn't go down.

Rules: your room is 18% of last year's earned income, up to $33,810 for 2026 (check your notice of assessment). Contribute by March 1, 2027 for 2026. It's a deferral: withdrawals are taxed later.

Next: tax instalments and the $3,000 rule.

Sources: CRA (canada.ca) RRSP limits; CRA T4127 2026. Example only; general information, not tax advice.

_vo: Put five thousand dollars into an R-R-S-P. How much of your tax bill goes away? Same freelancer: sixty thousand net, Manitoba. The bill was about sixteen thousand, one hundred. The R-R-S-P deduction cuts taxable income by five thousand. Federal tax drops seven hundred. Manitoba tax drops about six hundred and thirty-eight. New bill: about fourteen thousand, seven hundred and sixty-eight. You saved about one thousand, three hundred and thirty-eight. That's about twenty-seven cents per dollar. Not thirty-six. Why? Your C-P-P doesn't go down. It's based on your business income, not your taxable income. Your room is eighteen percent of last year's earned income, up to thirty-three thousand, eight hundred and ten. For twenty twenty-six, contribute by March first, twenty twenty-seven. And it's a deferral. You pay tax when you take the money out. Next: tax instalments, and the three-thousand-dollar rule. Follow so you don't miss it.
